Hello all! I am planning to open a PR (~160 lines) that establishes the link between the distance in the Cayley graph (realized as a SimpleGraph) and the word metric recently added to Mathlib/Geometry/Group/WordMetric.lean.

This implements TODO highlighted in #43118 and builds upon recent contributions of @Hang Lu Su to Mathlib/Geometry/Group.

I would love to get preliminary feedback and to check that no-one is already doing this.

Use of SimpleGraph vs Quiver/Schreier for Cayley graphs

This has been the subject of several discussions: 2022-2023, 2022-2024, 2025, 2026.
From what I can tell, the consensus is that both approaches are valid, but SimpleGraph currently has a more comprehensive API.
Nonetheless, it seems likely that a full Cayley graph and metric API will be added to Schreier graphs in the future.
To support future extensions, I'm including "Simple" in the names of definitions and theorems (e.g., cayleySimpleGraph). Please let me know if this is unnecessary.

Implementation outline

New file Mathlib/Geometry/Group/CayleySimpleGraph.lean

  • Group.Generators.cayleySimpleGraph : SimpleGraph G.
  • exists_walk_of_word: a word l gives a walk from g to g * P.wordProd l of length at most l.length.
  • exists_word_of_walk: a walk from g to h gives a word of the same length with value g⁻¹ * h.
  • dist_cayleySimpleGraph : P.cayleySimpleGraph.dist g h = P.wordLength (g⁻¹ * h).

Looking forward to your feedback!

Hi Dima,

I put this as a TODO because I indeed wanted to take a look eventually, but realistically I probably won't have time in the next month or so, so if you want to think about this and open a PR you're welcome to do so on my end. When I first started I was told the review process is the best way to get feedback.
Thank you! I've opened a PR for this: #44853.
